Use when the user wants to create or modify Solidity contracts that use OpenZeppelin — including token standards (ERC20, ERC721, ERC1155), access control (Ownable, AccessControl), security primitives (Pausable, ReentrancyGuard), or any OZ extension. Covers library-first integration, pattern discovery from installed source, and version-safe development.\"\n---\n\n# Develop Smart Contracts with OpenZeppelin\n\nAdapted from [OpenZeppelin's official skill](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-skills) for Scaffold-ETH 2 Solidity projects.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\nCheck if `./packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts` exists directly in the current working directory (do not search subdirectories). If it doesn't exist, this is not a Scaffold-ETH 2 project. Follow the instructions at https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/SKILL.md to scaffold it first. If it exists, continue directly with building.\n\nDetect the Solidity framework flavor:\n- If `packages/hardhat` exists → **Hardhat flavor**\n- If `packages/foundry` exists → **Foundry flavor**\n\n## Core Principle: Prefer Library Components Over Custom Code\n\nBefore writing ANY contract logic, search the installed OpenZeppelin library for an existing component:\n\n1. **Exact match exists?** Import and use it directly — inherit, override only what's needed\n2. **Close match exists?** Import and extend — override only functions the library marks as `virtual`\n3. **No match?** Only then write custom logic. Confirm by browsing the library's directory first\n\n**Never hand-write what the library already provides:**\n- Don't write `require(totalSupply() + amount <= cap)` when `ERC20Capped` exists\n- Don't write `require(msg.sender == owner)` when `Ownable` exists\n- Don't implement token transfer hooks manually when the library's base contracts handle it\n- Don't copy library source into your contract — always import from the dependency so the project gets security updates\n\n## Pattern Discovery: Read the Installed Source\n\nAPIs, override points, and import syntax change between major versions. Don't assume patterns from memory — always verify by reading the installed source.\n\n### Step 1: Identify the installed version and browse the library\n\nFind the OpenZeppelin version and locate the installed source:\n\n- **Hardhat**: check `packages/hardhat/package.json` for `@openzeppelin/contracts` version, then browse `packages/hardhat/node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/`\n- **Foundry**: check `packages/foundry/lib/openzeppelin-contracts/` and the remappings in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`\n\nBrowse the library's directory structure to discover available components. Key directories inside the OZ contracts root:\n- `token/{ERC20,ERC721,ERC1155}/` — token standards and their base implementations\n- `token/{ERC20,ERC721}/extensions/` — Capped, Burnable, Pausable, Permit, Votes, Enumerable, etc.\n- `access/` — Ownable, AccessControl, AccessManager\n- `utils/` — ReentrancyGuard, Pausable, math, structs\n\n### Step 2: Read the source file for the component you need\n\nLook at:\n- **Import syntax**: how the library's own files import each other — mirror that style. OZ v5+ uses named imports:\n  ```solidity\n  // ✅ import {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\n  // ❌ import \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\n  ```\n- **`virtual` functions**: only these can be overridden. Functions that were virtual in one version may not be in another\n- **Constructor parameters**: what must be passed during deployment\n- **NatSpec comments**: `NOTE: This function is not virtual, {X} should be overridden instead` — follow these\n\n### Step 3: Extract the minimal integration pattern\n\nFrom the source, identify only what's needed:\n- Imports to add\n- Inheritance chain\n- Constructor parameters and chaining\n- Required overrides (when inheriting multiple contracts that define the same virtual function, you must override it and call `super`)\n- New functions to expose\n\n### Step 4: Apply to the user's contract\n\nIntegrate into existing code. Check for conflicts: duplicate access control, incompatible inheritance, missing overrides. The Solidity compiler will error if two parent contracts define the same function and you don't explicitly override it.\n\n## SE-2 Integration Notes\n\n- OpenZeppelin is pre-installed in both flavors — no additional dependency installation needed\n- Contracts: `packages/hardhat/contracts/` (Hardhat) or `packages/foundry/contracts/` (Foundry)\n- Deploy scripts: `packages/hardhat/deploy/` (Hardhat) or `packages/foundry/script/` (Foundry)\n- Frontend reads contract ABIs from `packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` (auto-generated by `yarn deploy`)","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"ba6a5f0f-66bf-44ba-b1bf-721d033f0212","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:35:54.059Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"---\nname: openzeppelin\ndescription: \"Develop smart contracts using OpenZeppelin Contracts library. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMD9ME3VHs65NfyC2kkH","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01PQzuiW9MyQfB36JdJMYgDT","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T163343Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol","content":"//SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity >=0.8.0 <0.9.0;\n\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { SafeERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport { Ownable } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\nimport { ReentrancyGuard } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @notice A USDC tip jar. Anyone can leave a USDC tip with an optional message;\n *         the owner can withdraw the collected tips.\n * @dev The jar only ever holds and moves the ERC20 token passed at deployment\n *      (USDC on Base). Tippers must `approve` this contract for `amount` before\n *      calling `tip`, since the jar pulls funds with `transferFrom`.\n */\ncontract TipJar is Ownable, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice The ERC20 token accepted as tips (USDC).\n    IERC20 public immutable token;\n\n    /// @notice Longest tip message we store, to bound gas and calldata.\n    uint256 public constant MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 280;\n\n    struct Tip {\n        address from;\n        uint256 amount;\n        uint256 timestamp;\n        string message;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Every tip ever left, oldest first.\n    Tip[] public tips;\n\n    /// @notice Running total of all tipped amounts (token base units).\n    uint256 public totalTipped;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed from, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error MessageTooLong();\n    error NothingToWithdraw();\n\n    /**\n     * @param _token The tip token (USDC on Base: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913).\n     * @param _owner The address allowed to withdraw collected tips.\n     */\n    constructor(IERC20 _token, address _owner) Ownable(_owner) {\n        token = _token;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Leave a USDC tip with an optional message.\n     * @dev Requires a prior `token.approve(address(this), amount)` from the sender.\n     * @param amount Tip amount in token base units (USDC has 6 decimals).\n     * @param message Optional message shown in the tip feed.\n     */\n    function tip(uint256 amount, string calldata message) external nonReentrant {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (bytes(message).length > MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH) revert MessageTooLong();\n\n        // Pull the tip in before recording it (checks-effects-interactions).\n        token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n\n        totalTipped += amount;\n        tips.push(Tip({ from: msg.sender, amount: amount, timestamp: block.timestamp, message: message }));\n\n        emit NewTip(msg.sender, amount, message, block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw the full jar balance to the owner.\n    function withdraw() external onlyOwner nonReentrant {\n        uint256 balance = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n        if (balance == 0) revert NothingToWithdraw();\n\n        token.safeTransfer(owner(), balance);\n        emit Withdrawn(owner(), balance);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of tips in the feed.\n    function tipCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return tips.length;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Return the most recent tips, newest first.\n     * @param count Maximum number of tips to return.\n     */\n    function recentTips(uint256 count) external view returns (Tip[] memory) {\n        uint256 len = tips.length;\n        if (count > len) count = len;\n\n        Tip[] memory result = new Tip[](count);\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n            result[i] = tips[len - 1 - i];\n        }\n        return result;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":517,"cache_read_input_tokens":48191,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":517,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"5543889d-f3e2-497a-9517-3a2dba05449b","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:37:56.590Z","request_id":"req_011CdMD9L56JjdBGY1t48LNK"}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.19;\n\nimport \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport { ERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { Ownable } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\nimport { TipJar } from \"../contracts/TipJar.sol\";\n\n/// @dev Minimal 6-decimal stand-in for USDC used in unit tests.\ncontract MockUSDC is ERC20 {\n    constructor() ERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\") { }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 6;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\ncontract TipJarTest is Test {\n    MockUSDC internal usdc;\n    TipJar internal jar;\n\n    address internal owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address internal alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address internal bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    uint256 internal constant ONE_USDC = 1e6;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 100 * ONE_USDC);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 100 * ONE_USDC);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address who, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function testTipMovesUsdcAndRecordsFeed() public {\n        _tip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\");\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(alice), 95 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.tipCount(), ONE_USDC = 1e6;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 100 * ONE_USDC);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 100 * ONE_USDC);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address who, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function testTipMovesUsdcAndRecordsFeed() public {\n        _tip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\");\n\n Handles the ERC20 approve -> tip two-step: if the jar\n * is not yet approved for the entered amount, it approves first, then tips.\n */\nexport const TipForm = () => {\n  const { address: connectedAddress } = useAccount();\n  const { data: tipJar } = useDeployedContractInfo({ contractName: \"TipJar\" });\n\n  const [amount, setAmount] = useState(\"\");\n  const [message, setMessage] = useState(\"\");\n  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);\n\n  const { data: balance } = useScaffoldReadContract({\n    contractName: \"USDC\",\n    functionName: \"balanceOf\",\n    args: [connectedAddress],\n  });\n\n  const { data: allowance } = useScaffoldReadContract({\n    contractName: \"USDC\",\n    functionName: \"allowance\",\n    args: [connectedAddress, tipJar?.address],\n  });\n\n  const { writeContractAsync: writeUsdc } = useScaffoldWriteContract({ contractName: \"USDC\" });\n  const { writeContractAsync: writeTipJar } = useScaffoldWriteContract({ contractName: \"TipJar\" });\n\n  const parsedAmount = (() => {\n    try {\n      return amount ? parseUsdc(amount) : 0n;\n    } catch {\n      return null; // malformed input (too many decimals, letters, ...)\n    }\n  })();\n\n  const handleTip = async () => {\n    if (parsedAmount === null || parsedAmount <= 0n) {\n      notification.error(\"Enter a valid USDC amount\");\n      return;\n    }\n    if (balance !== undefined && parsedAmount > balance) {\n      notification.error(\"Amount exceeds your USDC balance\");\n      return;\n    }\n\n    setBusy(true);\n    try {\n      // Approve the jar for this tip if the current allowance is not enough.\n      if (allowance === undefined || allowance < parsedAmount) {\n        await writeUsdc({\n          functionName: \"approve\",\n          args: [tipJar?.address, parsedAmount],\n        });\n      }\n\n      await writeTipJar({\n        functionName: \"tip\",\n        args: [parsedAmount, message],\n      });\n\n      setAmount(\"\");\n      setMessage(\"\");\n    } catch (e) {\n      // errors are surfaced by the SE-2 transactor; nothing extra to do here\n      console.error(e);\n    } finally {\n      setBusy(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const disabled = !connectedAddress || busy || !parsedAmount;\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"card bg-base-100 shadow-xl w-full\">\n      <div className=\"card-body gap-4\">\n        <h2 className=\"card-title\">Leave a tip</h2>\n\n        <label className=\"form-control w-full\">\n          <div className=\"label\">\n            <span className=\"label-text\">Amount (USDC)</span>\n            {balance !== undefined && (\n              <span className=\"label-text-alt\">Balance: {formatUsdc(balance)} USDC</span>\n            )}\n          </div>\n          <input\n            type=\"number\"\n            min=\"0\"\n            step={`${1 / 10 ** USDC_DECIMALS}`}\n            placeholder=\"5.00\"\n            className=\"input input-bordered w-full\"\n            value={amount}\n            onChange={e => setAmount(e.target.value)}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <label className=\"form-control w-full\">\n          <div className=\"label\">\n            <span className=\"label-text\">Message (optional)</span>\n          </div>\n          <input\n            type=\"text\"\n            maxLength={280}\n            placeholder=\"gm, thanks for building!\"\n            className=\"input input-bordered w-full\"\n            value={message}\n            onChange={e => setMessage(e.target.value)}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <button className=\"btn btn-primary\" onClick={handleTip} disabled={disabled}>\n          {busy && <span className=\"loading loading-spinner loading-sm\" />}\n          {connectedAddress ? \"Send tip\" : \"Connect wallet to tip\"}\n        </button>\n\n        <p className=\"text-xs opacity-70\">\n          Tipping approves USDC for the tip jar (if needed) and then sends the tip in a second );\n};\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1179,"cache_read_input_tokens":64515,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1179,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":51,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"231fdcea-cd1e-4503-83b9-342091fcf7d3","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:41:10.970Z","request_id":"req_011CdMDPdCcmuyzsjv8UBfGu"}

// malformed input (too many decimals, letters, ...)\n    }\n  })();\n\n  const handleTip = async () => {\n    if (parsedAmount === null || parsedAmount <= 0n) {\n      notification.error(\"Enter a valid USDC amount\");\n      return;\n    }\n    if (balance !== undefined && parsedAmount > balance) {\n      notification.error(\"Amount exceeds your USDC balance\");\n      return;\n    }\n\n    setBusy(true);\n    try {\n      // Approve the jar for this tip if the current allowance is not enough.\n      if (allowance === undefined || allowance < parsedAmount) {\n        await writeUsdc({\n          functionName: \"approve\",\n          args: [tipJar?.address, parsedAmount],\n        });\n      }\n\n      await writeTipJar({\n        functionName: \"tip\",\n        args: [parsedAmount, message],\n      });\n\n      setAmount(\"\");\n      setMessage(\"\");\n    } catch (e) {\n      // errors are surfaced by the SE-2 transactor; nothing extra to do here\n      console.error(e);\n    } finally {\n      setBusy(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const disabled = !connectedAddress || busy || !parsedAmount;\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"card bg-base-100 shadow-xl w-full\">\n      <div className=\"card-body gap-4\">\n        <h2 className=\"card-title\">Leave a tip</h2>\n\n        <label className=\"form-control w-full\">\n          <div className=\"label\">\n            <span className=\"label-text\">Amount (USDC)</span>\n            {balance !== undefined && (\n              <span className=\"label-text-alt\">Balance: {formatUsdc(balance)} USDC</span>\n            )}\n          </div>\n          <input\n            type=\"number\"\n            min=\"0\"\n            step={`${1 / 10 ** USDC_DECIMALS}`}\n            placeholder=\"5.00\"\n            className=\"input input-bordered w-full\"\n            value={amount}\n            onChange={e => setAmount(e.target.value)}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <label className=\"form-control w-full\">\n          <div className=\"label\">\n            <span className=\"label-text\">Message (optional)</span>\n          </div>\n          <input\n            type=\"text\"\n            maxLength={280}\n            placeholder=\"gm, thanks for building!\"\n            className=\"input input-bordered w-full\"\n            value={message}\n            onChange={e => setMessage(e.target.value)}\n          />\n        </label>\n\n        <button className=\"btn btn-primary\" onClick={handleTip} disabled={disabled}>\n          {busy && <span className=\"loading loading-spinner loading-sm\" />}\n          {connectedAddress ? \"Send tip\" : \"Connect wallet to tip\"}\n        </button>\n\n        <p className=\"text-xs opacity-70\">\n          Tipping approves USDC for the tip jar (if needed) and then sends the tip in a second transaction.\n        </p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BkX4GnEDDG1ZsQiUr54uPX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n2\t\n3\t<h4 align=\"center\">\n4\t  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n5\t  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n6\t</h4>\n7\t\n8\t🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n9\t\n10\t> [!NOTE]\n11\t> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n12\t\n13\t⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n14\t\n15\t- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n16\t- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n17\t- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n18\t- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n19\t- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n20\t\n21\t![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n22\t\n23\t## Requirements\n24\t\n25\tBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n26\t\n27\t- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n28\t- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n29\t- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n30\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"50632575-38a0-4686-9d44-3b01d15eba2c","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:49:52.500Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T163343Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/README.md","content":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n","numLines":30,"startLine":1,"totalLines":83}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdME5aHcRx5yDXTwcuqck","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Gab86g1cbcY2twqHndruTH","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T163343Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/README.md","content":"# 💸 USDC Tip Jar on Base\n\nA tiny dApp that accepts **USDC tips on Base** and shows a live tip feed.\n\n- **Contract** — `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol`. Accepts tips in Base USDC\n  (`0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`), records a feed of\n  `(from, amount, timestamp, message)`, and lets the owner withdraw collected tips.\n- **Frontend** — `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. A tip form (approve → tip) plus the\n  live feed, jar totals, and an owner-only withdraw button.\n\nThe whole thing is developed and demoed **locally against a fork of real Base state**,\nso demo tips move real USDC between test identities with **no real money at risk**.\nProduction ships as a **static build on IPFS** — see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) — Node 22+/25 is fine\n- Yarn (this repo uses Yarn 4 via corepack)\n- [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil`, `cast`, `forge`)\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\nInstall dependencies once:\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n---\n\n## Local workflow: demo against real Base state\n\nEverything below runs on a **local Anvil fork of Base mainnet**. The fork has the real\nBase USDC contract and all of Base's real state, but it is exposed as **chain id 31337**\nand every account/balance is local — nothing you do touches mainnet or costs real money.\n\nYou need **three terminals** (from the repo root).\n\n### 1. Start a local fork of Base\n\n```bash\nyarn fork:base\n```\n\nThis runs `anvil --fork-url https://mainnet.base.org --chain-id 31337`. Leave it running.\n\n> Using your own Base RPC? Override it:\n> `yarn workspace @se-2/foundry fork:base` reads `BASE_RPC_URL`, e.g.\n> `BASE_RPC_URL=https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/<KEY> yarn fork:base`.\n\n### 2. Deploy the TipJar to the fork\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy\n```\n\n`DeployTipJar.s.sol` deploys `TipJar` pointed at the canonical Base USDC address (the\nsame address resolves on the fork). The deploy auto-exports the ABI + address to\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts`.\n\nThe deployer (Anvil account `#9`,\n`0xa0Ee7A142d267C1f36714E4a8F75612F20a79720`) becomes the jar **owner**.\n\n### 3. Start the frontend\n\n```bash\nyarn start\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:3000. The app targets the local fork (chain `31337`) by default and\nshows a **Burner Wallet** — that is your first test identity.\n\n### 4. Fund a test identity with USDC\n\nCopy your connected burner address from the top of the page, then fund it:\n\n```bash\n# from the repo root — AMOUNT is whole USDC (default 1000)\nyarn fund RECIPIENT=0xYourBurnerAddress AMOUNT=500\n```\n\nThis mints USDC **into the forked USDC contract's balance storage** for that address, so\nyou get spendable, real-contract USDC with no real money involved. It prints the new\nbalance to confirm. Refresh the app and your USDC balance appears in the tip form.\n\n### 5. Send a tip (moves real USDC between test identities)\n\nIn the tip form, enter an amount + message and click **Send tip**. The app:\n\n1. `approve`s the TipJar to spend that much USDC (only when the current allowance is too\n   low), then\n2. calls `tip(amount, message)`, which does a real USDC `transferFrom` from you into the\n   jar.\n\nThe tip appears instantly in the **Tip feed**, and **Collected in jar** updates.\n\n### 6. Demo a second identity\n\nOpen the **Burner Wallet** menu (top-right) and generate/switch to a new burner — that is\na second test identity. Fund it (step 4) and tip again. You now have real USDC moving\nbetween distinct test identities, all on the local fork.\n\n### 7. Withdraw (owner only)\n\nThe withdraw button only appears for the jar owner. To demo it, point the app at the\nowner account, or drive it from the CLI against the fork:\n\n```bash\ncast send <TIPJAR_ADDRESS> \"withdraw()\" \\\n  --private-key 0x2a871d0798f97d79848a013d4936a73bf4cc922c825d33c1cf7073dff6d409c6 \\\n  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545\n```\n\n(That key is Anvil account `#9`, the default local deployer/owner.) The jar balance goes\nto zero and the owner receives the collected USDC.\n\n---\n\n## Reset the demo\n\nStop `anvil` (Ctrl-C in terminal 1) and restart with `yarn fork:base`. A fresh fork wipes\nall local state (deployments, tips, funded balances). Re-run `yarn deploy`.\n\n---\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\nyarn test        # foundry unit tests for TipJar (mock 6-decimal USDC)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Project layout\n\n| Path | What |\n| --- | --- |\n| `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol` | The tip jar contract |\n| `packages/foundry/script/DeployTipJar.s.sol` | Deploy script (USDC address baked in) |\n| `packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol` | Unit tests |\n| `packages/foundry/Makefile` | `fork-base`, `fund-usdc` targets |\n| `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx` | Tip jar page |\n| `packages/nextjs/app/_components/` | `TipForm`, `TipFeed`, `JarSummary` |\n| `packages/nextjs/contracts/externalContracts.ts` | USDC token (ABI + address) |\n| `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts` | Target network (fork ↔ Base via env) |\n| `DEPLOY.md` | Production IPFS build + deploy + verification |\n\n---\n\n## How \"real USDC, no real money\" works\n\n- The local chain is a **fork** of Base: same USDC contract, same code, same on-chain\n  state — but it is a private copy running on your machine (chain id `31337`).\n- Funding uses an Anvil cheat (`anvil_setStorageAt`) to set a test account's USDC balance\n  on the fork. This is only possible locally and affects nothing on real Base.\n- The tip itself is a genuine ERC-20 `transferFrom` on the real USDC contract code, so the\n  demo exercises the exact same code path you'd hit on mainnet.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1242,"cache_read_input_tokens":116945,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1242,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"e16f15e4-62e2-44e3-bc5a-b81224ae5f19","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:50:30.909Z","request_id":"req_011CdME5VTQQ5YC7R4qn8LML"}

A tip form (approve → tip) plus the\n  live feed, jar totals, and an owner-only withdraw button.\n\nThe whole thing is developed and demoed **locally against a fork of real Base state**,\nso demo tips move real USDC between test identities with **no real money at risk**.\nProduction ships as a **static build on IPFS** — see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) — Node 22+/25 is fine\n- Yarn (this repo uses Yarn 4 via corepack)\n- [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil`, `cast`, `forge`)\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\nInstall dependencies once:\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n---\n\n## Local workflow: demo against real Base state\n\nEverything below runs on a **local Anvil fork of Base mainnet**. This is only possible locally and affects nothing on real Base.","+- The tip itself is a genuine ERC-20 `transferFrom` on the real USDC contract code, so the","+  demo exercises the exact same code path you'd hit on mainnet."]}],"originalFile":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n## Quickstart\n\nTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n\n1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n\n```\ncd my-dapp-example\nyarn install\n```\n\n2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n\n```\nyarn chain\n```\n\nThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n\n3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n\n```\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n\n4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n\n```\nyarn start\n```\n\nVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\nRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n\n- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n\n\n## Documentation\n\nVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n\nTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n\nPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdME8M8Bhh91MsT4PZZA9","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Wwb6XAc7Uqu2ngAhanxX2n","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T163343Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/DEPLOY.md","content":"# Production deploy — static site on IPFS + TipJar on Base\n\nProduction is a **static export** of the frontend, pinned to **IPFS**, talking to a\n**TipJar deployed on Base mainnet** (chain id `8453`). There is no server.\n\n> ⚠️ This document lists the exact commands. Running the IPFS upload **publishes the\n> build publicly** and deploying to Base **spends real ETH and moves real USDC** — only\n> run those steps intentionally, with a funded deployer you control.\n\n---\n\n## 0. Prerequisites\n\n- A deployer account with a little ETH on Base (for the contract deploy + gas).\n- A Base RPC URL (public `https://mainnet.base.org` works; a dedicated RPC is better).\n- API keys for the production frontend (recommended, not required for the build to run):\n  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALCHEMY_API_KEY`\n  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID`\n- `BASESCAN`/Etherscan v2 API key for contract verification (`ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`).\n\n---\n\n## 1. Deploy the TipJar to Base\n\nSet up a deployer keystore (skip if you already have one):\n\n```bash\nyarn generate            # creates a new encrypted keystore, OR\nyarn account:import      # import an existing private key\nyarn account             # print the deployer address + balances — fund it with Base ETH\n```\n\nDeploy and export the ABI/address into the frontend:\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy --network base\n```\n\nThis writes the deployed address into\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts` under chain id **8453**, so the\nproduction frontend can find it. Note the printed `TipJar` address.\n\n### Verify the contract on Basescan\n\n```bash\n# from packages/foundry — TipJar takes (IERC20 usdc, address owner)\ncd packages/foundry\nforge verify-contract <TIPJAR_ADDRESS> contracts/TipJar.sol:TipJar \\\n  --chain base \\\n  --constructor-args $(cast abi-encode \"constructor(address,address)\" \\\n      0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 <OWNER_ADDRESS>) \\\n  --etherscan-api-key $ETHERSCAN_API_KEY \\\n  --watch\ncd ../..\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Build the static site (targets Base)\n\nThe build is driven entirely by env vars — no code edits:\n\n- `NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true` → `next.config.ts` switches to `output: \"export\"`,\n  `trailingSlash: true`, and unoptimized images (all required for IPFS).\n- `NEXT_PUBLIC_TARGET_NETWORK=base` → the app targets Base mainnet (`8453`) instead of the\n  local fork.\n\nBuild only (produces `packages/nextjs/out/`, uploads nothing):\n\n```bash\nNEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TARGET_NETWORK=base \\\nNEXT_PUBLIC_ALCHEMY_API_KEY=<key> \\\nNEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID=<id> \\\nyarn workspace @se-2/nextjs build\n```\n\nSanity-check the output before uploading:\n\n```bash\nls packages/nextjs/out/index.html          # must exist\nnpx serve packages/nextjs/out              # optional: preview at http://localhost:3000\n```\n\nBecause the export uses `trailingSlash` and relative assets, it works from any IPFS\ngateway subpath.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Upload to IPFS\n\nPick one. **Neither is run automatically — run it when you're ready to publish.**\n\n### Option A — one shot (build + upload) with bgipfs\n\n```bash\n# builds with NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true and uploads packages/nextjs/out\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TARGET_NETWORK=base yarn ipfs\n```\n\nThis prints the resulting CID and a gateway URL like\n`https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>`.\n\n### Option B — upload an already-built `out/` yourself\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nyarn bgipfs upload config init -u https://upload.bgipfs.com   # first time only\nyarn bgipfs upload out\n# -> prints \"CID: <CID>\"\ncd ../..\n```\n\nOr with a local Kubo node / a pinning service (Pinata, web3.storage, …):\n\n```bash\nipfs add -r --cid-version 1 packages/nextjs/out   # the root CID is the last line\n```\n\n**Record the CID** — that is your immutable site version.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Post-deploy verification\n\nRun these after uploading. Replace `<CID>` and `<TIPJAR_ADDRESS>`.\n\n```bash\n# 1. The site is retrievable from IPFS and returns the app HTML (HTTP 200).\ncurl -sI \"https://<CID>.ipfs.dweb.link/\" | head -n 1\ncurl -s  \"https://<CID>.ipfs.dweb.link/\" | grep -o \"USDC Tip Jar\"\n\n# 2. A second gateway resolves the same CID (content is really pinned/propagated).\ncurl -sI \"https://ipfs.io/ipfs/<CID>/\" | head -n 1\n\n# 3. The TipJar exists on Base and points at the right USDC token.\ncast call <TIPJAR_ADDRESS> \"token()(address)\"  --rpc-url https://mainnet.base.org\n# expect: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\ncast call <TIPJAR_ADDRESS> \"owner()(address)\"  --rpc-url https://mainnet.base.org\n\n# 4. Frontend is wired to the same address the app will call.\ngrep -A2 '\"8453\"' packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts | grep -i address\n```\n\nThen, in a browser pointed at `https://<CID>.ipfs.dweb.link/`:\n\n- The page loads, styles/blockies render (assets resolved over IPFS).\n- Connecting a wallet on **Base** shows your USDC balance.\n- A small real tip goes through (`approve` → `tip`) and appears in the feed; the\n  transaction is visible on https://basescan.org.\n- The owner’s **Withdraw** button transfers collected USDC to the owner.\n\n---\n\n## Updating the site later\n\nIPFS content is immutable — any change produces a **new CID**. Rebuild (step 2), re-upload\n(step 3), and re-verify (step 4). If you front the site with IPNS or a DNSLink domain,\nrepoint it at the new CID so the human-friendly URL always serves the latest build.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2611,"cache_read_input_tokens":118187,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2611,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e62e52ec-5b78-40b5-b0d0-709aeeea5ce7","uuid":"bb99c853-e077-4e84-8a8a-a4439be6ed1d","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:51:17.865Z","request_id":"req_011CdME8KhrRg9zSTTKcjjcD"}
